text:
incident-bot: P1 page -> customer: Newton Systems. Detected widespread 401s for VPC tenants using mTLS. Auto-created bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident/2443210000. Paging alice-oncall :rotating_light:

alice-oncall: Seeing spike in auth failures from newton-prod. Errors start ~23:06 UTC. 401s and `x509: certificate has expired` in the auth-proxy logs.

newton-sre: Confirmed. We rotated our intermediate CA yesterday but the rotation pipeline didn't push the full chain to the tenant keystore. Some backend services still present the old chain.

alice-oncall: Thanks. Quick triage: which path fails — ingress mTLS to auth-proxy or downstream to tenant bridge?

charlie-sre: From early logs looks like handshake fails at the mutual TLS verification step at our VPC ingress proxy. snippet from auth-proxy logs: `2026-03-14T23:06:12Z auth: authz error: tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate (x509: certificate has expired)`

ben-sre: I pulled the cert chain from one failing client with `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect lb.newton.internal:8443` and the intermediate is expired: `Not After : Mar 13 12:00:00 2026 GMT`. Confirmed.

carmen-ops: Impact? Which customers affected and percentage of requests?

alice-oncall: Only Newton tenant(s) on their VPC peering + Dedicated Bridge. Traffic for that tenant ~12% of their prod requests hitting our regional pool eu-west-1. We see ~95% of their auth attempts failing starting at 23:05.

eve-cse: Pinged Newton: they see downstream errors and some jobs failing. On their side they can re-provision immediate certs but want to coordinate so we don't flail.

dmitri-runtime: Short-term mitigations we can do from our side: 1) enable tenant-level auth fallback (token-based) for Newton so their workloads keep running while they finish cert roll. 2) add a temporary exception to accept the chain if leaf cert valid (not ideal security-wise). 3) route Newton traffic to a dedicated non-mTLS pool if they can accept it.

alice-oncall: Let's not do #2 (chain accept) unless Newton explicitly signs off. Prefer #1 or #3. Newton, can you temporarily allow token-only auth for service-to-service?

newton-sre: We can flip to token-based for a few hours. Will need the API key we use for service tokens; do you want us to call your support endpoint or do you need us to supply the keys?

eve-cse: We'll coordinate keys over the bridge. Newton will generate a short-lived token and we'll add it to their tenant config via the private control plane.

ben-sre: Operational play: I can push a canary change to their tenant policy to enable token fallback (policy flag `vpc.mtls_fallback: token`). Patch will be on the control plane and should take effect in ~30s for new connections. I can also add a route to redirect new sessions to eu-west-2 burst pool if Newton prefers non-mTLS.

alice-oncall: Action list:
- Newton: re-issue intermediate and push full chain to tenant keystore (primary fix).
- Ben: enable token fallback on control plane (short-term).
- Carmen: open customer incident ticket and log SLA impact.
- Charlie: keep trace logs and attach handshake samples to postmortem.
- Dmitri: prepare rollback and config for pool routing if token fallback fails.

ben-sre: Starting token-fallback change now. Patch id: CP-98321. Watch metric `vpc.auth_fails.newton` and `vpc.token_accepts.newton`.

incident-bot: NOTE: Zoom bridge recording started, timeline created, on-call handoff pending.

(30s later)

ben-sre: Token-fallback enabled. New auth attempts now show token evaluation. `vpc.auth_fails.newton` dropped from 95%->8% in 2m.

newton-sre: We're spinning the cert re-issue job now. ETA ~18 minutes for our CA pipeline to publish new intermediate and update keystore. We'll push once ready.

alice-oncall: Good. Carmen, please send the initial incident severity update to Newton execs: include ETA and our mitigation steps; mark service impact window starting 23:05 UTC.

carmen-ops: Sending now. Also filing a temporary SLA credit calc; numbers: 12% of Newton prod traffic affected for 18m => estimated customer impact 3.6% of monthly requests.

charlie-sre: Captured sample handshake logs and attached to the incident: `auth-proxy-23-06.log` showing chain and expired intermediate.

(17m later)

newton-sre: New intermediate pushed to keystore and validated. They updated keystore via API: `PUT /v1/tenants/newton/keystore` with new PEM bundle. We tested `openssl s_client` and chain now returns `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`.

ben-sre: Rolling changeset to remove token-fallback and restore strict mTLS. Reverting CP-98321.

dmitri-runtime: Watch for error spike when we flip back. I'll standby to route to burst pool if handshake regression occurs.

(2m later)

ben-sre: Revert done. `vpc.auth_fails.newton` flatlined at ~0.6% (normal noise).

alice-oncall: Customer confirms services recovered. Newton ops will do a post-change validation of all service certificates and will coordinate with us to add automated chain checks to their pipeline.

carmen-ops: Closing bridge in 30 minutes unless anyone objects. Filing post-incident ticket and schedule for postmortem runbook.

charlie-sre: POV for postmortem: root cause = partial intermediate rotation; contributing = no chain-validation step in their CI, and our onboarding docs didn't emphasize verifying full chain presence. Action items: 1) update onboarding to require `openssl verify -CAfile` checks, 2) provide a preflight check in our control plane to validate cert chains during uploads, 3) add alerting to detect sudden spikes in `x509: certificate has expired` errors per tenant.

alice-oncall: Agreed. Also add doc note on when token-fallback is acceptable and the approval flow.

newton-sre: Thanks to the team for quick response. We'll send our internal RCA and timeline once we validate all services.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED by alice-oncall at 2443210462. Postmortem scheduled at 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
